description: End-to-end verification boundaries for the NetworkX common-subtree Python APIs: graph and callback encoding, original-node and path witnesses, 2016/2018 empty and rooted policies, f64 versus exact rational semantics, PyO3 and ABI3 packaging, the compiled verified ordered Lean backend, tested public behavior, and feasible compositional proof interfaces.

related_resources.reason: Mathematical ordered common-tree relation underlying the separately proved rational ordered isomorphism backend.
2016 weighted nonempty isomorphism objective and its different public empty-allowed convention.
2018 path-embedding validity, direct-edge reward, skipped-vertex penalty and returned original paths.
Functional correctness statements, theorem hypotheses, finite witness validity, and the limits of source execution guarantees.

learning_objectives: Specify successful, empty and error outcomes of the 2016 and 2018 public NetworkX APIs independently of implementation
Explain graph/label/weight encoding and original-node indexed-witness reconstruction, including path interior vertices and rooted policy
Work a concrete 2018 embedding through Python result generation, rescoring and the 2016 strict-isomorphism comparison
Distinguish f64 numerics, callback None, zero weight, +infinite skipping penalty and exact ordered rational affinities
Identify what RationalSolver.solveResult_correct, the restricted Rust token source theorems and weighted unordered tests actually establish
Explain why PyO3/ABI3 compatibility and result rescoring do not imply source-level optimality
Decompose a proposed end-to-end correctness and error contract into separately provable encoding, solver, decoding and numerical links
